ingredient_lines.original_text: 3 cups dried red peas (kidney beans) or gungo peas (pigeon peas)
2 cups coconut milk or 1 packet coconut powder
1 bunch scallions or 1 small white onion, chopped

ingredient_lines.note: white or brown, rinsed and drained
ingredient_lines.original_text: 1 ½ lb white or brown rice, rinsed and drained

steps: Wash the beans in clean water. Put them in a pot with the water, salt and garlic, stir, and leave to soak overnight.

Put the pot of beans and their liquid on the hob, cover and bring to the boil over a medium heat, then boil hard for 10 minutes, as dried kidney beans must. Lower the heat and simmer, stirring now and then, until the beans are tender, about 20 minutes. Add more hot water if the level drops too low.
Lower the heat, then add the coconut milk, Scotch bonnet, spring onions, thyme, margarine, all-purpose seasoning, seasoned salt and chicken seasoning, and stir well.
Cover and boil over a medium heat for 10 minutes.
Stir in the rice until evenly spread through. Cover, lower the heat and cook until the rice is soft and the liquid has gone, about 10 to 15 minutes.
Serve.

recipes.title: Tres leches cake
recipes.description: A light sponge soaked in three milks (condensed, evaporated and cream) until rich and damp, then piled with meringue and toasted under the grill.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

lines.original_text: ½ tsp cream of tartar (optional but used for stabilizing the egg whites; increasing their heat tolerance and volume)

steps: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan). Grease and flour a cake tin.
Whisk the 5 egg whites in a stand mixer until frothy, bringing the mixer up to its fastest speed slowly and pausing for a minute at each speed.
Slowly beat in the sugar and vanilla.
Mix in the egg yolks, then the flour.
Pour the batter into the tin and bake for 20 minutes.
Leave the cake to cool to room temperature, then poke holes all over it.

For the milk mixture, put the condensed milk, evaporated milk, cream and vanilla in a pan and heat for 5 minutes, stirring all the time. It only needs to bring the flavours together, so don't let it get too hot.
Leave the milk mixture to cool to room temperature.
Slowly pour the milk mixture over the cake. Because the tin is greased, the milk flows around and under the cake, which soaks up most of it.
For the meringue, put the 3 egg whites in the stand mixer and bring it up to its fastest speed slowly, pausing for a minute or so at each speed.
Add the cream of tartar, then slowly beat in the sugar.
Spread the meringue over the cake.
Toast the meringue gently with a blowtorch or under the grill. Once it starts to colour you have only a few seconds before it burns, so watch it closely.

recipes.title: General Tso's chicken
recipes.description: Crisp battered chicken thigh tossed in a sticky, sweet and sour sauce of dark soy, rice vinegar, ginger, garlic and dried chillies, the Chinese-American takeaway favourite.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured
recipes.photo_author: Rick Audet from Holyoke, Massachusetts, USA

lines.original_text: 750 g (1.65 lb) raw chicken dark meat, boneless and skinless.

lines.note: for deep-frying, or enough to shallow-fry
lines.original_text: 700 ml (3 cups) oil to deep fry, or enough oil to shallow-fry

steps: Cut the chicken into 2 cm cubes.
Beat the egg, light soy sauce, salt and pepper in a bowl. Add the chicken, then stir in the cornflour to thicken the batter.
Mix the sauce ingredients in another bowl, stirring out any lumps, and set aside.

Heat the oil in a wok (to 180°C if deep-frying). Fry the battered chicken a few pieces at a time until crisp, about 3 minutes; if shallow-frying, fry until the chicken is cooked through and the batter golden. Drain off the excess oil.
Empty and wipe out the wok, add 2 tbsp of the oil and return it to the heat. Stir-fry the spring onions and chillies for about 30 seconds.
Return the chicken to the wok and stir-fry with the vegetables until browned.
Stir the sauce and add it to the wok. Once it boils, cook for about a minute, until it thickens; how long depends on how much cornflour you added.
Take off the heat and serve straight away, with steamed or fried rice.

recipes.title: Meat and shrimp potstickers
recipes.description: Northern Chinese dumplings filled with pork, prawns, water chestnuts, ginger and coriander, fried until crisp underneath, then steamed in the same pan.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

lines.original_text: ½ pound (about 250 g) ground chicken or pork
½ pound ground raw prawn or shrimp

lines.note: fresh if possible, peeled and sliced
lines.original_text: ½ cup water chestnuts (fresh if possible) peeled and sliced

lines.note: mixed into water to seal, if you like

steps: Mix together all the filling ingredients.
Put a small bowl of water on the work surface; stir in a little cornflour if you like, to make a glue.
Lay out a wrapper, moisten its edges with a wet finger and put a heaped teaspoon of filling in the middle. Fold the wrapper over the filling and pinch the edges to seal. Repeat with the rest.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a large frying pan or wok. Add the dumplings carefully and fry over a high heat until golden underneath, about a minute.

Without turning them, add the 250 ml water and cover. Steam for about a minute to cook the filling, then turn off the heat so the bottoms do not burn, and leave the dumplings to finish cooking for a few more minutes.
Serve with a dipping sauce or soy sauce.

recipes.title: Soy mustard lamb chops
recipes.description: Lamb chops marinated in soy, mustard, honey, rosemary and sesame, then seared over a fierce heat and basted with the marinade as they cook.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured
steps: Mix the marinade ingredients together.
Slash the fat side of the chops and add them to the marinade, coating the sides as well as each flat face. Leave to marinate for about 30 minutes, turning often.
Heat a barbecue or grill until very hot.
Lift the chops out of the marinade, keeping the marinade, and sear them on one side for 3 minutes.
Dip each chop in the marinade on both sides and return it to the heat, uncooked side down. Cook for another 3 minutes to sear.
Dip the chops in the marinade again and cook for 1 minute on a lower heat, covered if you are using a barbecue with a lid. Repeat on the other side and serve straight away.

recipes.title: Boeuf bourguignon
recipes.description: Chunks of beef browned and braised for hours in red wine with onions, garlic, carrots, mushrooms and a bundle of herbs.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.original_text: 1 kg beef (blade steak or stewing shoulder cut)

ingredient_lines.note: a few sprigs, tied in a bundle with the rosemary and thyme
ingredient_lines.original_text: Bouquet of herbs: basil, rosemary and thyme tied with string
Bouquet of herbs: basil, rosemary and thyme tied with string
Bouquet of herbs: basil, rosemary and thyme tied with string

steps: Cut the beef into large 5 cm chunks and season with salt, pepper and olive oil.
Brown the beef a little at a time in a casserole or large saucepan until golden brown all over. Lift out each batch as it is done and set aside.
Add the onions and garlic to the same pan and cook until golden brown.
Sprinkle over the flour and cook for a few minutes longer.
Pour in half the red wine, bring to the boil, then simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the beef, carrots, herbs and mushrooms.
Pour in the rest of the wine and enough water to cover the meat and vegetables.
Simmer for 2 to 3 hours, stirring now and then and skimming off any scum from the surface.

recipes.title: Flammekueche
recipes.description: An Alsatian flatbread of thin yeasted dough spread with crème fraîche, soft onions and nutmeg, dotted with bacon and baked in a very hot oven.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

lines.original_text: ¼ cup moderately hot water, about 110 °F (45 °C)
1 medium (3 oz / 85 g) onion, finely chopped
1 cup crème fraîche, commercial or home made (see note)

steps: Mix the starter ingredients in a small bowl, cover tightly and leave somewhere warm for 30 minutes.
When the starter is light and bubbly, stir in the beer and milk.

Put the flour and salt in a food processor and, with the motor running, pour the yeast mixture through the feed tube. Process until the dough forms a ball, adding a very little extra flour or milk if needed.
Keep processing until the dough is smooth, elastic and warm, 45 seconds to 1 minute.
Butter a medium bowl, roll the dough around in it, cover and leave somewhere warm until doubled in size. Knock it back and leave it to rise a second time.
While the dough rises, heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a non-stick frying pan. Cook the onion over a low heat, stirring, for 5 minutes or until golden brown. Leave to cool.
Mix the crème fraîche with the salt, pepper and nutmeg, then stir in the cooled onion.
Heat the rest of the oil in the pan and fry the bacon, stirring constantly, until lightly browned. Drain in a sieve.
Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan), or as hot as it will go. If you use a pizza stone, heat the oven for at least 30 minutes.
Lightly oil a 35 × 40 cm baking tray. Roll out the dough a little smaller than the tray and lay it on. If you use a pizza stone, you can roll the dough out on a sheet of baking paper instead.
Spread the onion mixture over the dough, leaving a very small rim all round, then dot with the bacon.
Bake for 4 to 20 minutes, depending on your oven, until lightly browned and bubbling. Blackened edges are traditional. Serve very hot.

recipes.title: Tartiflette
recipes.description: Waxy potatoes, crisp bacon and soft onions cooked down with white wine and cream, baked under a halved reblochon until it melts.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.note: waxy, 5 or 6 medium, all the same size
ingredient_lines.original_text: 1¾ pounds Yukon Gold potatoes (5 or 6 medium-sized ones, all the same size) or waxy boiling potatoes

ingredient_lines.note: in a piece, or salt pork, cut into lardons
ingredient_lines.original_text: 5–6 ounces slab bacon or salt pork, cut into lardons about 1 x ¼ x ¼ inch
1 ea. (about 6 ounces) medium onion, finely chopped
¼ cup dry white wine or dry vermouth
6 tablespoons (¼ cup plus 2 tablespoons) heavy cream
½ tsp salt, or to taste

steps: Boil the potatoes in their skins for exactly 20 minutes, until they are just beginning to get tender. Do not overcook them. Rinse with cold water to stop the cooking.
While the potatoes cook, cut the bacon into slices about 1 cm thick, then into lardons about 1 cm across.
While the potatoes are still warm, peel them with your fingers and cut them into slices about 1 cm thick, then into rough cubes.
Melt the butter in a large sauté pan and cook the lardons over a medium-high heat until crisp and golden brown. Lift them out with a slotted spoon, leaving the fat in the pan.
Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan).
Cook the onion in the bacon fat over a medium heat, stirring often, until soft and lightly golden. Drain in a sieve, pressing with a spoon to remove as much fat as you can.
Pour the fat out of the pan, return the bacon and onion and add the wine. Cook over a high heat until the wine has nearly evaporated.
Add the potatoes and cook for a minute or so, stirring constantly, until everything is well mixed.
Add the cream, salt and pepper; it takes a little more salt than you might think, at least ½ tsp. Stir together for a minute.
Lightly butter a 25 to 28 cm earthenware baking dish. Add the potato mixture and smooth the top.

Cut the reblochon in half from top to bottom into two half-moons and keep one for another use. Lightly score the rind of the other half every 2.5 cm, including the side, then slice it horizontally through the middle into two thinner half-moons.
Lay the two pieces rind side up on the potatoes so they make a round of cheese again.
Cover the dish tightly with foil and bake in the middle of the oven for 1 hour.
Take off the foil and stir the cheese, rind and all, into the potatoes.
Put the dish 13 to 15 cm under a hot grill and cook until golden brown on top.

recipes.title: Teurgoule
recipes.description: A Norman rice pudding of round-grain rice, sugar and cinnamon baked slowly in milk for five hours until a dark skin forms on top.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured
steps: Heat the oven to 150°C (130°C fan).
Mix the sugar, milk, rice, salt and cinnamon in an ovenproof dish.
Bake for 5 hours without opening the oven door. The rice should absorb about three-quarters of the milk and be covered by a brown skin.
Leave the pudding to cool and serve at room temperature.

recipes.title: Black Forest gateau
recipes.description: The German celebration cake: a cocoa shortcrust base and a light chocolate sponge layered with kirsch-spiked cherries and whipped cream, finished with shaved chocolate.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

lines.original_text: Butter, cut into pieces: ¼ cup, 50 g

lines.note: 3 drops of bitter almond oil, or 2 tsp almond extract
stoned, from a jar or tin
lines.original_text: Sour cherries, stoned: 1 can, 24 oz (750 g)
Shaved chocolate for garnish: 40 g (2 oz)

lines.note: 1 jar, or maraschino cherries, to decorate
lines.original_text: Glacé or maraschino cherries for decoration: 1 jar

steps: For the base, mix the flour, cocoa and baking powder in a bowl and make a well in the middle. Mix the egg white with the sugar and vanilla sugar, pour it into the well and stir in some of the flour until it forms a thick paste.
Add the cold butter and rub it in, then mix in the rest of the flour and knead briefly into a ball. Chill for 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 160°C (140°C fan). Roll the dough out to fit the base of a 20 cm springform tin, press it in and bake for 20 minutes.
For the cake, whisk together the flour, cornflour, baking powder and cocoa.
Whisk the 4 egg yolks with the warm water until foamy, then gradually whisk in two-thirds of the sugar, the vanilla sugar, almond extract and cinnamon.
Whisk the egg whites to stiff peaks, then whisk in the rest of the sugar a little at a time. Fold the whites into the yolk mixture, then sprinkle over the flour mixture and fold it in carefully.

Pour into a 20 cm springform tin lined with baking paper and bake at 160°C (140°C fan) for about 35 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean. Cool in the tin for 15 minutes, then turn out onto a wire rack to cool completely.
For the filling, drain the cherries in a sieve, keeping the juice. Heat three-quarters of the juice in a saucepan and mix the cornflour into the rest.

When the juice boils, stir a little of it into the cornflour mixture, then stir it all back into the pan and cook until thickened. Stir in the sugar until dissolved, then the cherries. Take off the heat, leave to cool and stir in the kirsch.
Sprinkle the gelatine over the cold water and leave for 10 minutes, stirring now and then. Warm it gently until melted, then leave to cool to room temperature without letting it set.

Whip the cream to soft peaks and fold in the cool, still-liquid gelatine. Whip until stiff, adding the vanilla sugar and the sugar to taste. If you have no vanilla sugar, use 1 tbsp vanilla extract and sugar to taste.
To assemble, spread half the cherry mixture and a third of the cream over the base. Cut the cake horizontally into two layers with a length of cotton thread and press one onto the filling.
Spread over the rest of the cherries and half the remaining cream, top with the second layer of cake and spread the rest of the cream over the top.
Scatter with the shaved chocolate, decorate with the cherries and chill for at least 4 hours before serving.

recipes.title: Lentil and sausage stew
recipes.description: A Swabian-style stew of brown lentils cooked with smoked pork belly, frankfurters and potatoes, finished with a brown roux sharpened with red wine vinegar.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.note: for the lentils; don't use more, as the liquid becomes the sauce
ingredient_lines.original_text: 1 litre water for the lentils (needed for the sauce; don't use more)
2 pairs of scalded sausage, whole or in pieces
1 large piece of smoked pork belly

steps: Rinse the lentils in a sieve, then cook them over a low heat in the litre of water for 40 to 50 minutes.
About 20 minutes before the end, add the carrot, onion, potatoes, garlic, sausages, bay leaf and pork belly. When the lentils are done, set the pot aside and keep it warm.
For the roux, melt the butter in a small pan, add the flour and cook carefully until brown, stirring all the time.
Gradually stir in the 500 ml of water and bring to the boil. Add the tomato purée, vinegar and honey, and season with the salt and pepper.
Stir the sauce into the lentils, mix well and keep warm. Take out the bay leaf before serving.

recipes.title: Moussaka
recipes.description: Layers of fried aubergine and a rich lamb or beef sauce scented with cinnamon and red wine, topped with a cheesy béchamel and baked until golden.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

lines.original_text: 1 kg (2.2 lbs) minced/ground beef or lamb
1 large tin (28 oz/800 g) diced tomatoes
Sprinkle of nutmeg, cinnamon, and black pepper
Sprinkle of nutmeg, cinnamon, and black pepper
Sprinkle of nutmeg, cinnamon, and black pepper
½ cup (120 ml) freshly-grated Parmesan cheese
1 cup (250 ml) grated cheese (e.g. Edam, etc.)

steps: Cut the aubergine into 5 mm slices, lay them out and sprinkle generously with salt. Leave for at least an hour to draw out the bitterness.
For the meat sauce, heat the olive oil in a saucepan and fry the onion and garlic until the onion starts to colour. Add the mince and brown it thoroughly.
Add the bay leaves and cinnamon stick and keep stirring until all the moisture from the meat has gone.
Add the tomatoes, tomato purée, sugar, parsley, basil and pepper. Mix well and cook for 15 minutes, stirring now and then.
Add the wine and cook until the sauce is very thick, with very little liquid left. Take out the bay leaves and cinnamon stick and leave to cool.

For the cheese sauce, melt the butter in another saucepan over a low heat. Take it off the heat and stir in the flour, then return to the heat and cook gently for 3 minutes, stirring all the time so it doesn't catch.

Take off the heat and stir in the milk, then bring to the boil and cook gently for 1 minute, stirring all the time. Take off the heat, stir in the cheeses, nutmeg, cinnamon and pepper, and leave to cool.

Rinse the aubergine slices under running water and pat dry on kitchen paper. Heat olive oil in a frying pan, turn the slices in the hot oil to coat both sides and fry until soft and coloured. Drain and repeat with the rest.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Cover the base of a large ovenproof dish with aubergine slices, then add a layer of meat sauce. Repeat until the dish is full to within 3 cm of the top.
Mix the egg into the cool cheese sauce, spoon it over the top layer and sprinkle with a little extra grated cheese. Bake for 45 minutes, then leave to cool and set for 10 minutes before serving.
Serve with a Greek salad, red wine and crusty garlic bread.

recipes.title: Chapati
recipes.description: Soft wholemeal flatbreads, kneaded from just flour, salt and warm water and cooked on a hot dry pan until puffed and speckled brown.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.original_text: Warm water as required (about 1 ½ cups)

steps: Mix the flour and salt, then knead in the water, starting with a little and adding more as you go, until the dough is smooth but not too sticky.
Cover the dough and leave it to rest for at least 5 minutes.
Divide the dough into balls and roll each out into a thin disc, a little thicker than denim, sprinkling with flour as you roll.
Put an unoiled frying pan over a fairly high heat and test how hot it is by holding your hand over it.
When it is very hot, put a chapati in the pan and press it flat with a spatula or a dry cloth to make it puff up.
Turn it over and repeat, so it is lightly browned on both sides.
Brush with ghee, if you like.

recipes.title: Dal makhani
recipes.description: A rich Punjabi dal of whole black urad and kidney beans, simmered soft then finished with a spiced tomato masala, cream and ghee.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

lines.original_text: 1 cup whole dried urad dal (skinless black gram)

steps: Wash the urad dal and kidney beans and leave them to soak overnight in plenty of lukewarm water.
Drain, then cook the dal and kidney beans in the water with the salt, chilli powder, turmeric and grated ginger until soft. Boil briskly for the first 10 minutes, so the kidney beans are safe to eat.
Set the cooked dal aside.

Heat the ghee or oil in a heavy-based pan. Add the asafoetida, bay leaves, cinnamon stick, cloves and onion and cook until light golden brown. When the onion turns brown, add the ginger garlic paste and fry.
Add the tomatoes and fry, then add the ground coriander. Fry until the tomatoes have broken down.
Add the cooked dal, with water as needed.
Mix well and simmer for 15 to 20 minutes.
Add the cream and the ghee and simmer for 5 minutes. Take off the heat, season with salt and scatter over the coriander.
Serve hot with naan, paratha or rice.

recipes.title: Indian butter chicken
recipes.description: Chicken marinated in yoghurt and tandoori masala, then simmered with butter-softened onions, warm spices, tomato and cream.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.note: skinless and boneless, or breast; about 800 g on the bone
ingredient_lines.original_text: 400–500 g of skinless, boneless chicken thighs or breasts (with the bone, this will probably be 800 g)

steps: Trim the chicken and cut it into small cubes. If you prefer chicken on the bone, cut long, thin slashes across it instead.
In a large bowl, mix the tandoori masala, yoghurt and lemon juice with the chicken. Massage it well with your hands so the chicken is evenly coated, then cover and leave for at least 30 minutes.
Heat a large saucepan or frying pan until evenly hot.

Melt the butter in the pan until it froths. Add the onion and cinnamon and fry gently. When the onion is soft and starting to brown, stir in the garlic and ginger, then the turmeric, chilli powder and ground coriander, and fry over a medium heat.
Add the chicken and fry, stirring all the time, until it has turned white. This is quick, so take care not to overcook it.
Stir in the tomato purée, then add the cream and heat through. If you like, add more tandoori masala to taste; 3 to 5 tbsp is usually enough.
Cover and simmer for just over 10 minutes.

recipes.title: Matar paneer
recipes.description: Golden fried paneer and peas in a smooth spiced onion and tomato gravy, finished with a sizzling chilli oil.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.original_text: 8 oz (200 g) paneer, cut in 1” cubes
3 green chilies, seeded and finely chopped

steps: Heat some of the oil in a deep pan. Fry the paneer cubes over a medium-low heat until golden brown on all sides. Lift out and drain on kitchen paper.
Pour off the excess oil from the pan and add the ginger garlic paste, then the onion. Cook, stirring, until the onion is translucent.
Add the tomatoes and mix. Cook over a medium heat until the tomatoes have given up all their water, then take off the heat and leave to cool.
Tip the mixture into a blender, add the green chillies and blend until smooth.
Heat more oil in the pan. Add the cumin seeds and fry until they crackle. Add the turmeric, half the chilli powder, the ground coriander and the garam masala and mix well over a low heat.
Add the blended purée and mix well over a medium heat. Season with the salt, then mix in the peas.
Add the water, cover and cook until the peas are tender.
Uncover, add the fried paneer and mix well, adding more water if needed.
For the tadka, heat 1 tsp of the oil in a small pan, stir in the rest of the chilli powder, then turn off the heat. Pour it over the matar paneer and scatter with the coriander to serve.

recipes.title: Pohe
recipes.description: A quick Maharashtrian breakfast of flattened rice steamed in the pan with mustard seeds, turmeric, green chillies and soft onion.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured
steps: Put the poha in a bowl and hold it under a slow-running cold tap to moisten it. Mix by hand, drain off the excess water and set aside; don't let it soak too long or it turns pasty.
Heat the oil in a frying pan until medium hot. Add the mustard seeds and let them crackle for a few seconds.
Add the turmeric and asafoetida and fry for a few seconds, taking care not to burn the turmeric.
Add the green chillies and fry for a few seconds.
Add the onion and lower the heat. Cover and cook for 2 minutes, until the onion is soft but not brown.
The poha should have soaked up its excess water by now. Loosen it by hand so the flakes don't stick together, and add it to the pan.
Season with salt and stir so the turmeric colours the poha evenly.
Cover and cook over a low heat for 5 minutes without lifting the lid, so the poha cooks in the steam.
Stir and cook for another minute, uncovered.
Serve in bowls, scattered with the chopped coriander.

recipes.title: Caponata
recipes.description: A Sicilian sweet-and-sour stew of fried aubergine, celery, tomatoes, olives, capers and pine nuts, served cold with fresh basil.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.original_text: ½ pound (225 g) green olives packed in brine, pitted

steps: Strip the strings from the celery and blanch it in lightly salted water for 5 minutes. Drain, cut into bite-sized pieces, fry in a little oil and set aside.
Wash and dice the aubergine, sprinkle it generously with salt and leave in a colander for several hours to draw out the bitterness. Meanwhile, blanch, peel, deseed and chop the tomatoes.

Rinse the salt off the aubergine and pat it dry. Thinly slice the onion and fry it in olive oil until translucent, then add the capers, pine nuts, olives, tomatoes and the passata, if using. Cook, stirring with a wooden spoon, for about 15 minutes until the tomatoes are done, then take the pot off the heat.
While the tomatoes cook, heat oil in another pan and fry the aubergine in batches so the oil stays hot. Return the tomato pot to the heat and stir in the aubergine and the celery.
Cook over a low heat for a few minutes, stirring gently, then stir in the vinegar and sugar. When the vinegar has almost evaporated, take off the heat and leave to cool.
Serve cold, garnished with fresh basil. It keeps for several days in the fridge.

recipes.title: Italian meatballs
recipes.description: Tender veal meatballs bound with breadcrumbs, egg and parmesan, seasoned with garlic and herbs, browned in a pan and finished in the oven.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.original_text: 500 g (18 oz/1½ lb) minced veal meat
30 g (1 oz/1 Tbsp) grated Parmesan cheese

steps: Mix all the ingredients except the oil in a large bowl, squeezing them together with your hands.
Heat a large frying pan over a medium heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Meanwhile, heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan).
Roll the meat into bite-sized balls with your hands.
Put the meatballs in the pan and cook uncovered for 3 minutes, then turn them over and cook for another 3 minutes.
Move the meatballs to a baking tray and bake for 20 to 25 minutes.

recipes.title: Ossobuco alla Milanese
recipes.description: Veal shins browned and slowly braised in white wine and stock with soft vegetables, tomato, anchovy and lemon peel until the meat falls from the bone.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.note: slices from the hind leg, 2.5–4 cm thick
ingredient_lines.original_text: 4 slices veal hind shank, about 2.5–4 centimeters (1–1½ inches) thick
3 ribs celery with leaves, chopped fine
240 ml (1 cup) dry white wine or white vermouth

steps: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan). If the butcher hasn't done it, tie each shin round the middle with kitchen string so it keeps its shape.

Choose a heavy casserole with a lid that just fits the shins in one layer. Put in the butter, 2 tbsp of the oil, the onion, celery and carrot and sweat over a medium heat for about 8 minutes until softened. Add the garlic and lemon peel and cook for 2 minutes more until fragrant. Take off the heat.
Meanwhile, heat the rest of the oil in a frying pan until almost smoking. Dust the shins lightly with flour and brown them well on both cut sides, then lay them on the vegetables in the casserole.
Pour the wine into the frying pan and boil until reduced by half, scraping up the bits from the bottom. Pour it over the veal.

Bring the stock to the boil in the frying pan and whisk in the tomato purée and anchovies. Add it to the veal with the thyme, bay leaves, a few grinds of pepper and the large pinch of salt. The liquid should come three-quarters of the way up the shins; if not, add water.

Bring to a simmer, cover and cook in the oven for about 2 hours, turning and basting the shins every half hour. If the liquid nearly evaporates, add hot water about 120 ml at a time. The veal is done when it is tender and falling from the bone.
Lift the shins onto a platter, remove the string and cover to keep warm. If the sauce is watery, boil it on the hob over a high heat until thick and creamy. Pour it over the veal and serve.

recipes.title: Panna cotta with red fruit sauce
recipes.description: Cool, wobbly Italian cream and milk puddings set with gelatine, turned out and served with a quick sauce of blended red berries.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

lines.note: such as strawberries, raspberries or blueberries

steps: Stir the gelatine into the cold water and leave to soak for about 5 minutes.
Put the milk, cream, sugar and soaked gelatine in a pan. Bring to a gentle boil, stirring regularly so it doesn't catch, then take off the heat.
Pour into small dessert moulds and chill for 2 to 3 hours until set.
Meanwhile, blend the berries with the sugar to make the sauce.
To serve, turn each panna cotta out onto a plate and spoon over the red fruit sauce.

recipes.title: Spaghetti alla carbonara
recipes.description: The Roman classic: spaghetti tossed with crisp-edged guanciale or pancetta, egg yolks, pecorino and parmesan into a glossy sauce, with plenty of black pepper.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.original_text: 178 ml (¾ cup) grated Pecorino Romano cheese

steps: Dice the guanciale or pancetta into 2.5 cm pieces.
Bring a large pot of water to the boil, salting it to taste as it starts to simmer. Cook the spaghetti until al dente, then drain, keeping 240 ml of the cooking water.

While the spaghetti cooks, heat the oil in a large frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add the pancetta, turn the heat down low and cook for about 10 minutes, until it has given up most of its fat but is still chewy and barely browned.
In a bowl, slowly whisk about 120 ml of the pasta water into the egg yolks, then add the grated cheeses and mix well with a fork.
Tip the drained spaghetti straight into the frying pan with the pancetta, toss and turn off the heat.
Add the egg and cheese mixture to the pasta, stirring in the rest of the pasta water to loosen the sauce into a smooth emulsion.
Add the pepper and toss everything together to coat the pasta.

recipes.title: Miso soup
recipes.description: A light Japanese soup of miso dissolved in water with sesame-fried spring onions, and tofu, mushrooms, prawns and seaweed as you like.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.original_text: ½ cake tofu (optional), cut into ½-inch cubes

ingredient_lines.note: a few pieces, or other seaweed

steps: Heat the oil in a small pan.
Add the spring onions and cook for a few minutes, stirring often.
Add 600 ml of the water and bring to the boil.
Dissolve the miso in the remaining 125 ml of water and add it to the pan.
Lower the heat and add the mushrooms, prawns, seaweed and tofu, if using. Simmer gently for a few minutes until the prawns are cooked through.

recipes.title: Tonkatsu
recipes.description: Japanese breaded pork cutlets: beaten thin, coated in flour, egg and panko, fried until deep golden and served in strips with a sweet and tangy sauce.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured
recipes.photo_author: yoppy from Tonkatsu Restaurant Houraitei in Shibuya, Tokyo

lines.original_text: 2 pork cutlets (boneless pork loin chop), about 1 cm thick

steps: For the sauce, beat equal parts of soy sauce, sugar, Worcestershire sauce and ketchup together with a fork until smooth. Chill for half an hour to thicken, if you like.
Put the pork in an open freezer bag to stop it splashing and beat it with a meat mallet until about 5 mm thick. Season both sides with the salt and pepper.
Put the flour, beaten egg and breadcrumbs in separate shallow bowls. Coat the pork completely in the flour, then the egg, then the breadcrumbs.
Heat about 1 cm of oil in a frying pan. Drop in a few crumbs to test it: when they float and sizzle, the oil is ready.
Fry the pork for a few minutes on each side until deep golden brown.
Cut into strips with a sharp knife and serve with Japanese short-grain rice, thinly shredded cabbage and the sauce.

recipes.title: Quesadillas
recipes.description: Two flour tortillas melted together in a pan around grated cheese and whatever you have to hand: salsa, chillies, tomatoes and coriander, spinach, beans or leftover meat.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

lines.original_text: 2 flour tortillas, 6 inches (15 cm) in diameter

lines.note: grated, ideally a mix of Monterey Jack and cheddar, or a Tex-Mex blend
lines.original_text: ⅓ cup grated meltable cheese (preferably a Monterey Jack and cheddar blend or a Tex Mex blend)

lines.note: as salsa criolla, a Peruvian onion relish
or other cooked meat or seafood
washed and torn into small pieces
lines.original_text: Fresh spinach, washed and torn into small pieces
Canned black beans, rinsed and well drained

steps: Warm both tortillas in the microwave until they bend easily, and keep one warm.
Heat a frying pan or griddle over a medium-low heat. Grease it with oil or cooking spray and put one tortilla in the pan.
Scatter the cheese over the tortilla.
Top the cheese with about 4 tablespoons of any mix of the fillings, ideally warmed and very well drained, spread evenly across the tortilla.
Let the cheese melt. The tortilla may brown in spots, but it shouldn't change colour much.
Press the other tortilla on top, making sure it sticks a little.
Turn the quesadilla over and warm it until it holds together.
Take it out of the pan and cut it into 8 wedges.
Eat straight away, or keep it somewhere warm that is not hot enough to melt the cheese.

recipes.title: Koshary
recipes.description: Egypt's favourite street food: layers of rice, lentils, macaroni and chickpeas under a sharp cumin and tomato sauce, topped with crisp fried onions.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

lines.original_text: 1 teaspoon ground black pepper, more to taste
1 teaspoon white wine vinegar, more to taste

steps: Soak the chickpeas and lentils in water overnight.
Boil the rice, the drained chickpeas and the drained lentils, each until tender. Cook the macaroni until al dente. Drain them all.
In a container with a lid, layer the rice, the lentils, the macaroni and then the chickpeas. This is the koshary base.
Fry the onion in the olive oil until crisp. Drain off the excess oil if you like, and keep the onion for the topping.
Mix the tomato purée and water in a saucepan. Put it over a medium-high heat and stir in the cumin, black pepper and vinegar.
Cook the sauce until most of the liquid has evaporated.
Add some warm or hot water and simmer over a low heat. You can blend it with a stick blender for a smoother sauce.
To serve, scoop about 350 ml of the base into each bowl, pour over some sauce and top with 1 tbsp of the fried onion.
Add more vinegar and black pepper to taste, and serve.

recipes.title: Lahoh
recipes.description: Spongy Yemeni flatbreads from a yeasted semolina and flour batter, cooked on one side only until the top is full of holes.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.original_text: 3 cup of wheat flour or sorghum flour
Dab of margarine or vegetable oil for greasing pan

steps: Mix the semolina with 125 ml of the lukewarm water in a saucepan and bring to the boil. Take off the heat, tip into a bowl and leave to thicken.
Stir in the cold water.
Stir in the salt until it has dissolved.
Stir in the flour and yeast.
Mix in the remaining 475 ml of lukewarm water to make a thin batter.
Cover the batter and leave it until it has risen and is bubbly.
Grease a frying pan with a little oil or margarine and heat it over a medium heat.
Ladle some batter into the pan and let it spread out. A little flour sprinkled in the pan helps stop it sticking.
Cook until the top is covered in holes like a sponge. Turn it over and cook for about 5 seconds, then lift out and leave to cool. Repeat with the rest of the batter.

recipes.title: Maqluba
recipes.description: A simple Palestinian pot of rice cooked with allspice-browned beef mince and onion, served with cool yoghurt.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured
steps: In a saucepan, brown the beef mince and onion in a little olive oil with salt, black pepper and allspice; use more allspice than pepper. Take off the heat.
Add the rice and water and bring to the boil over a medium heat.
Turn the heat down to medium-low and cover, with the lid tilted to let some steam escape.
When most of the water has gone and the surface of the rice is pitted, put the lid on tight and cook over a low heat for 15 minutes.
Take off the heat and leave covered for 2 to 3 minutes. Serve with yoghurt.

recipes.title: Mejadra
recipes.description: Lentils and rice, each toasted in olive oil with warm spices and simmered, then mixed and piled with deeply golden fried onion.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.original_text: 1 cup (80 g / 2.8 oz) uncooked rice or bulgur

steps: Fry the lentils in a little olive oil for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring all the time, until the first ones start to scorch.
Season with salt, baharat, cumin and cardamom to taste.
Add 500 ml of the water and cover. Bring to the boil, then lower to a simmer and cook for 20 minutes, or until the lentils have soaked up all the water.
In another pan, fry the rice in a little olive oil for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring all the time, until the grains change colour.
Season with salt, pepper and cardamom.
Add the remaining 500 ml of water and cover. Bring to the boil, then lower to a simmer. After 5 minutes turn off the heat and leave to stand for another 10 minutes.
Cut the onion into thin strips, about 0.5 by 4 cm.
Fry the onion in olive oil until crisp and deeply golden brown. This takes a while but gives a much fuller flavour.
Mix the lentils and rice and top with the fried onion. Use 2 parts lentils to 1 part rice for a moist mix.

recipes.title: Tabbouleh
recipes.description: A fresh, herb-heavy Levantine salad of finely chopped parsley, mint, tomatoes and spring onions with soaked bulgur and plenty of lemon.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.original_text: ½ cup bulghur wheat (fine grind is best, medium grind acceptable)
2 bunches parsley (flat leaf or curly Italian)
Romaine lettuce leaves (garnish and scoopers, optional)

steps: Soak the bulgur wheat in at least three times its volume of cold water. Fine bulgur needs only 30 minutes; medium needs longer. It has already been parboiled, so it needs no cooking.
Drain the bulgur.
Chop the parsley leaves, spring onions, mint, tomatoes and cucumber.
Chop the parsley quite finely, with a knife rather than a food processor.

Mix the vegetables and bulgur together and pour over the strained lemon juice. If you are not serving straight away, cover and keep somewhere cool. Add the salt and olive oil only just before serving.
Serve with lettuce or vine leaves around the bowl, to scoop up the salad.

recipes.title: Moroccan salad
recipes.description: A fresh chopped salad of ripe tomatoes, green pepper and onion with coriander and cumin, sharpened with vinegar or lemon and left to mingle.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.original_text: 1 handful of fresh coriander, finely chopped

steps: Cut the tomatoes, pepper and onion into small dice.
Add the coriander, cumin, salt, pepper and vinegar.
Put everything into a container, put the lid on tightly and give it a good shake to combine.
Leave to rest for 30 minutes so the flavours mingle before serving.

recipes.title: Paella valenciana
recipes.description: Valencia's own paella: chicken and rabbit browned in olive oil, simmered with beans, tomato, paprika and saffron, then cooked with short-grain rice until a crisp socarrat forms.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.note: or duck, cut into small pieces

ingredient_lines.original_text: 250 g (10 ounces) chopped green bell peppers (optional)
500 g (17.5 ounces) diced or grated tomatoes
125 g (4.5 ounces) large haricot beans (canned or fresh)
100 g (3.5 ounces) small haricot beans (canned or fresh)
125 g (4.5 ounces) fresh runner beans or green beans

ingredient_lines.note: 8–10 threads, and/or 1½ tsp yellow food colouring
ingredient_lines.original_text: 8–10 threads of saffron and/or 1½ teaspoons yellow food coloring (see notes)
400 g (14 ounces) calasparra rice, bomba rice, or pearl rice

steps: Clean the snails, chicken and rabbit well. Cut the chicken and rabbit into small pieces and salt them generously.
Heat the olive oil in a paella pan and fry the chicken and rabbit until golden brown.
Add the green pepper and fry for 1 minute, then add the garlic and fry until brown, taking care as garlic burns easily.
Add the paprika, then quickly add the tomatoes so the paprika doesn't burn. Fry until the tomatoes are dark and pulpy and the mixture has reduced a little.

Add the water and bring to a rolling boil. Add the snails, fresh butter and haricot beans (tinned ones go in later), runner beans and saffron. Boil over a high heat for 10 minutes. Sweep a rosemary sprig through the broth for no more than 30 seconds, then take it out.
Taste the broth and add more salt, a pinch at a time, if it needs it.
Add the rice and stir it in, then spread it evenly over the pan in a layer about 1 cm deep. Cook over a high heat for 10 minutes.
Turn the heat down to medium and simmer for 4 minutes. Add any tinned beans, turn the heat down low and simmer for 4 minutes more, tasting the rice often: it is done when slightly firm to the bite.
There should be some toasted rice stuck to the bottom of the pan, the socarrat. If not, turn the heat up high and listen for the rice crackling.
Take the pan off the heat when the rice is almost dry, lay the remaining rosemary sprigs on top, cover with a clean white tea towel and leave for 5 minutes before serving.

recipes.title: Thai chicken fried rice
recipes.description: Street-style khao pad gai: chilled jasmine rice stir-fried hard with chicken, egg, tomato and onion, seasoned with fish sauce and served with cucumber and lettuce.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.original_text: 1 large chicken breast, sliced in thin strips

ingredient_lines.note: Thai jasmine, cooked and chilled overnight
ingredient_lines.original_text: 4 cups (900 g) cooked Thai jasmine rice, refrigerated overnight
½ yellow onion, chopped into strips
¾ roma tomato, cut into strips
¾ cup (180 g) cilantro, finely chopped

lines.note: peeled; score down the sides with a fork if you like
lines.original_text: 3 slices cucumber, peeled (note: can run fork down all sides lightly if desired)

steps: Prepare all the ingredients and set them out in small bowls by the hob.
Heat about 4 tbsp oil in a wok over a high heat. When it is almost smoking, add the chicken and stir it about vigorously.
When the chicken starts to brown, push it up the side of the wok and crack in the eggs. Stir them a little; when almost scrambled, mix in the chicken and stir for 30 seconds more.
Push the eggs and chicken aside, add a little more oil and stir-fry the tomato and onion for about 5 minutes. They will not look done yet, but they will be fine in the end.
Add the cold rice and mix everything together.

Turn the heat to low and add a few splashes of fish sauce and soy sauce, to taste. Add the sugar, salt, a splash of vinegar, and the MSG and chilli sauce if using. Scatter the fried garlic on top, stir it all in and turn off the heat.
Arrange the garnishes on a lettuce leaf on a large platter, plate the fried rice beside them and eat the garnishes with the rice.

recipes.title: Thai green chicken curry
recipes.description: Chicken simmered in coconut milk with green curry paste, lime leaves and lemongrass, finished with coriander and a squeeze of lime.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.original_text: 2 tbsp Thai green curry paste (according to taste)

ingredient_lines.note: thick stalks, fat ends bashed with a rolling pin
ingredient_lines.original_text: 1–2 thick stalks lemongrass, fat ends bashed with a rolling pin (optional)

ingredient_lines.note: skinless and boneless breast and/or leg, cut into chunks
ingredient_lines.original_text: 750 g (1½ lb) skinless, boneless chicken, cut into chunks (use breast and/or leg meat)

ingredient_lines.note: torn, or the grated zest of 1 lime
ingredient_lines.original_text: 6–8 kaffir lime leaves, torn into pieces (if unavailable, use the grated zest of 1 lime)

ingredient_lines.note: a good shake, or light soy sauce
ingredient_lines.original_text: 1 good shake of Thai fish sauce or light soy sauce
1 small handful of coriander leaves, roughly chopped

steps: Heat the oil in a wok or large frying pan.
Add the curry paste and sugar and cook over a fairly high heat for about a minute, stirring with the lemongrass if using.
Lower the heat slightly and stir in the chicken and lime leaves or zest until coated in the paste.
Add the coconut milk and the fish sauce or soy sauce and bring to a simmer. Cook for 25 to 30 minutes until slightly thickened.
Stir in the coriander and lime juice, then taste and add more fish sauce or soy sauce if needed.
Leave the curry to sit for a few minutes so the sauce becomes creamier and the flavours of the paste come through. Serve with plenty of Thai jasmine rice.

recipes.title: Tom yum soup with chicken
recipes.description: Tom yum gai: a hot and sour Thai broth with chicken, straw mushrooms, lemongrass, lime leaves and bird's eye chillies, sharpened with lime juice and fish sauce.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.original_text: 400 grams (about 1 lb) boneless chicken meat, diced
1 fresh lemongrass stem, cut into short lengths
5–6 hot fresh Thai chilies, just broken with pestle

steps: Put the stock in a pan with the lemongrass and lime leaves and bring to the boil over a medium heat.
Add the chicken, mushrooms, fish sauce, lime juice and sugar and cook gently, uncovered and without stirring, for 10 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and chillies and cook for 5 minutes more, then take off the heat.
Serve with steamed jasmine rice.

recipes.title: Dolma
recipes.description: Vine leaves, onions, courgettes, peppers, tomatoes and cabbage leaves stuffed with spiced beef and rice, layered in one pot and simmered in a sharp citrus liquid.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

lines.original_text: 2 pounds coarse or minced raw chuck roast
1 can tomato purée or 3 fresh tomatoes

steps: Blanch the vine leaves: put them in a pan of boiling water, cover with a tea towel and cook for 3 to 5 minutes.
Cut each onion at the root end and slit it lengthwise by 1 cm. Boil for 5 to 10 minutes until soft, then separate the layers without tearing them.
Slice the courgettes lengthwise and hollow them out.
Core the cabbage and boil it for 10 minutes, then pull the leaves apart ready for stuffing.
Hollow out the chillies, tomatoes and peppers, keeping their tops.
Mix all the stuffing ingredients together in a large bowl.

Stuff the vine leaves: lay each leaf shiny side down and put a tablespoon of stuffing at the bottom centre by the stem. Fold the bottom of the leaf up over the stuffing, fold in the sides and roll it up into a cylinder.

Stuff the tomatoes and peppers and put their tops back on. Stuff the other vegetables, rolling the onion layers and cabbage leaves tightly around the stuffing. Stuff them all a little loosely so the rice has room to swell.

Layer the stuffed vegetables in a large pot, with the courgettes on their sides and the onions and tomatoes upright, alternating with layers of stuffed vine leaves; the top layer should be vine leaves.
Mix the citric acid with the water and pour it over, just to cover the top layer of leaves. Put a small plate upside down directly on top as a weight.

Cover the pot and cook over a high heat for about 10 minutes, until it boils. Lower the heat to medium and simmer for about 40 minutes, until most of the liquid is absorbed and the rice and meat are cooked.
Take off the heat and leave to stand for 10 minutes.
Remove the lid and plate. Put a large platter over the pot and, wearing oven gloves, turn the pot out onto the platter. Arrange the dolma as you like and serve.

recipes.title: Beef pho
recipes.description: Vietnam's beef noodle soup: a clear broth simmered for hours from beef bones, charred onion, ginger and warm spices, poured over rice noodles and raw sirloin.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

lines.original_text: 2 large white onions, cut into quarters

lines.note: with a little meat on them
lines.original_text: 5 lbs beef bones (choose ones with a bit of meat on them)

lines.note: thin and flat, soaked in hot water until soft and drained
lines.original_text: Phở noodles (thin, flat rice noodles), soaked in hot water until soft and drained
Finely sliced beef sirloin (ask your butcher)

steps: Fry the onions in the oil until lightly browned, then lift out and drain.
Rinse the beef bones, put them in a stockpot, cover with cold water and bring slowly to the boil. Lower the heat and simmer, uncovered, for 10 to 15 minutes, skimming off the foam for a clear broth.

Add the fried onions, ginger, cinnamon, cardamom, star anise, cloves and peppercorns. Bring back to the boil, then simmer gently, partly covered, for at least 6 hours and up to 12 if you can, skimming regularly. Top up with water if needed to keep the bones covered.
Strain the broth, discarding the bones, vegetables and spices, and return it to the hob to keep it boiling hot.

Put a handful of noodles in each large soup bowl, top with the raw sliced beef and ladle over plenty of the very hot broth, which cooks the beef. Garnish with the sliced onion, spring onions and coriander and serve straight away.

Put the chillies, beansprouts, lime wedges and basil on a large plate for everyone to add as they like, with the fish sauce, chilli sauce, hoisin sauce and pepper for adding to the soup or dipping the meat and noodles.
